$comment: Single source of truth for the container images and the MCP servers they
carry. Consumed by docker/render.py, which renders venv/servers.tsv (read by
venv/run), the mcpServers block of .claude-plugin/plugin.json, the in-image
server map and the build matrix of .github/workflows/build-images.yml.
Adding a server means editing this file and re-rendering.
Every image installs uv projects from their venv/<venv>/uv.lock, the same
locks a host install uses, so a container is the same environment with a
newer glibc and the build tools already present:
venvs  - several projects side by side, one per server, on a CUDA
toolkit image that compiles what has no wheel for the platform

images.name: cpu
images.notes: No torch. Carries every optional extra the architecture allows (openmm, docking; pymol on amd64 only).

images.name: mlip
images.notes: torch 2.14 with the CUDA 13 build (the host picks CUDA 12.6 on older drivers). Cannot host fairchem: mace-torch pins e3nn==0.4.4, fairchem-core needs e3nn>=0.5.

images.name: fairchem
images.notes: torch 2.13 (fairchem-core requires torch~=2.13) with the CUDA 13 build.

images.name: generative
images.notes: arm64 only: on x86_64 these servers run from their uv projects on the host (PyG publishes x86_64 wheels). The image compiles torch-scatter/sparse/cluster with CUDA for TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST (GB10: sm_121).
